derivedNote: These values apply arithmetic to numbers the source already publishes; they add no new source claims.
missingNone: The source provides all of these.
conditionHint: Original-source conditions only; missing details do not match. These filters do not predict the best recipe for your beans.
equipmentIntro: Source-backed specifications, compatibility notes and related recipes for drippers, kettles, grinders, filter paper and espresso machines.
equipmentNote: Specifications follow official brand pages. Unspecified models are not guessed.
heroSubtitle: Explore original recipes. Find your next cup.
homeDescription: A free, nine-language library of source-backed pour-over recipes from leading coffee authors and competitors, with original sources, versions and verification dates.
quickAnswer: Quick answer: {dose} g ground coffee, {water} {unit} water, {temperature}, grind {grind}, total time {time}.
faqAmountQuestion: How much coffee and water does {recipe} use?
faqTemperatureQuestion: What water temperature and grind does {recipe} use?
author: Author
sectionIntro: Original methods, carefully sourced. Browse by equipment, explore an author, or compare recipes side by side.
limit: You can compare up to three recipes.
compareSubtitle: Original parameters, side by side. See the differences clearly.
compareNote: Units are preserved as published. Water volume in mL is not silently converted to mass in g.
compareEmpty: Choose recipes from the library to begin a comparison.
invalidSelection: Some recipes in this link are unavailable, duplicated or exceed the three-recipe limit. Only valid selections are shown.

ratioConverter.title: Scale this recipe
ratioConverter.intro: Keep the source ratio. Change coffee or water, and the other amount updates.
ratioConverter.status: Scaled to {dose} g coffee and {water} {unit} water.
ratioConverter.sourceText: The author's steps below keep their original numbers; the timeline and step amounts show your scale.
ratioConverter.caveat: Timing, grind and pouring rhythm stay unchanged. Large changes can alter flow and extraction.
ratioConverter.unavailable: This recipe includes a range, upper limit, ice or source formula, so automatic scaling is withheld to avoid treating several possible brews as one fixed ratio.

sourceIntro: Every recipe links to its creator or a publishing partner. Versions remain separate; missing details are shown explicitly.
methodText: Measurements stay in their published units. Equipment filters find matching equipment, not a personal best recipe. Fixed amounts are not automatically scaled.
translationNote: Translations are independently prepared and terminology-checked. The linked original remains the reference; no creator endorsement is implied.
imageNote: Editorial images are AI-generated illustrations, not photographs supplied by the recipe authors.
independent: An independent coffee reference by imycc.

siteInfo.aboutIntro: A free, independent library of source-backed pour-over recipes and brewing equipment.
siteInfo.aboutPurpose: The library collects publicly published recipes from baristas, competition broadcasts and brands. Each entry keeps its original source, version and checking date so you can return to the maker's own method.
siteInfo.aboutPrinciples: We keep source units and unknowns visible, separate versions, and do not invent missing values or imply that one method is best.
siteInfo.aboutIndependence: This is an independent reference. It is not affiliated with recipe authors or equipment brands, and trademarks remain with their owners.
siteInfo.contributeText: You can suggest recipes, report broken links, correct equipment facts or improve translations through the project repository.
siteInfo.termsIntro: Basic conditions for using this free recipe library.
siteInfo.termsUse: You may use the recipes for personal brewing and learning. Content is provided as it is, without a promise that it is complete, current or suitable for your equipment.
siteInfo.termsAccuracy: Recipes and equipment facts are checked against linked sources, but errors and source changes can happen. Check the original source and manufacturer instructions for important details.
siteInfo.termsResponsibility: Use care when handling hot water, blades, electricity and coffee equipment. This site is not legal, medical or safety advice.
siteInfo.termsRights: Recipe authors, publishers and equipment brands keep their own rights. Names and trademarks are used only to identify sources and products.
siteInfo.privacyIntro: This site is designed to avoid unnecessary data collection.
siteInfo.privacyData: There are no accounts, comment forms or newsletter sign-ups, so the site does not ask for your name, email address or payment details.
siteInfo.privacyAnalytics: Page views use GoatCounter, which records anonymous, aggregate visit information. See GoatCounter's privacy policy for current details.
siteInfo.privacyExternal: Source, video, GitHub and analytics sites have their own policies. Review them before sharing information with those services.

authorsIntro: Explore each author’s published recipes and original sources.
noResults: No recipes match these filters. Try another brewer or clear the filters.
raoWater: The source gives its own preferred figures, without a stated reporting basis.
raoPrep: With the valve open, rinse the filter and drain the rinse water. Fit the barrel firmly, add the coffee and level the bed.
derived: Total water is calculated from the source’s dose and stated mass ratio, not a separately published measurement.

instruction.bloom: Add the stated amount to wet the coffee grounds.
instruction.pour: Add the stated amount at the indicated time. The total so far is shown separately.
instruction.pause: Stop pouring until the next step begins.
instruction.close: Close the valve immediately after the first pour.
instruction.open: Open the valve after topping up.
instruction.topup: Pour until the water sits about 1 cm above the grounds.
instruction.pulses: Use short pours to keep the water 1–2 cm above the grounds, continuing to the total water target.
instruction.level: Level the coffee bed before brewing.
instruction.drain: Stop pouring and let the water level drop a little.
instruction.grind: Grind immediately before brewing, straight into the basket.
instruction.dose: Dose the stated amount of coffee.
instruction.tamp: Tamp level and with steady pressure.
instruction.lock: Lock the portafilter firmly into the group head.
instruction.preinfuse: Start a low-pressure pre-infusion for the stated time.
instruction.extract: Raise to brew pressure and extract to the stated yield.
instruction.stop: Stop the shot at the stated yield or time.
instruction.purge: Rinse the group before locking in.

kodama.title: Hiroyuki Kodama · ORIGAMI Air
kodama.summary: Four pours with Wave paper and C40 MK4.
kodama.notes: 320 g water; approximately 265 g beverage. Total time is unspecified.
kodama.finish: Remove just before dripping stops; about 265 g beverage. No fixed time.
kodama.prep: Rinse with cold water. Grind 28 g at 25 clicks, remove fines using Saza M and blow off chaff. Use 21 g of prepared grounds.
kodama.water: Tajima natural water supplied at the event.

kobayashi.title: Tsuyoshi Kobayashi · ORIGAMI S
kobayashi.summary: Wave paper, Red Clix and a cooler final pour.
kobayashi.notes: 2024 third place. First round: 56 Red Clix clicks; final: 55. Last pour: approximately 75°C.
kobayashi.finish: Remove at 2:30 and mix gently with a spoon.
kobayashi.prep: Grind at 55 Red Clix clicks and sift to obtain 15 g. Rinse and fit the paper into the grooves with a pin, preheat the bowl and level the bed with a pin.
kobayashi.first: Pour gently and evenly over the bed.
kobayashi.last: Lower kettle water to approximately 75°C; use a thin, slow centre pour.
kobayashi.water: Tajima natural water was provided at the venue; the reporting basis for the hardness is not given.

selorio.title: Lui Selorio · ORIGAMI Air
selorio.summary: ZP6 Special and CAFEC paper with four pours; only the first three interval ends are clear from the source.
selorio.notes: Overview: 240 mL; steps: g. Third interval says 1:00–1:00, so only the start time is retained.
selorio.third: Begin the third 60 g pour at 1:00. The source labels this interval 1:00–1:00, so its end is unknown rather than a ten-second pour.
selorio.s00: Pour 50 g of water over ten seconds, then wait until 0:30.
selorio.s01: Pour 70 g of water over ten seconds, then wait until 1:00.
selorio.s03: Pour the last 60 g over ten seconds and let the water draw down until 2:25.

rincon.title: Janer Joseph Perez Rincon · ORIGAMI
rincon.summary: Natural Geisha with Sibarist and varying water temperatures.
rincon.notes: Exact pour times, first temperature, roast and total time are unspecified. Later temperatures are shown per step.
rincon.water: Source: Pure Colombian Water; mineral composition unspecified.
rincon.s00: First pour: 50 g of water. The card gives no temperature or time for this pour.
rincon.s01: Second pour: 70 g of water at 92 °C; no time is published.

gil.title: Milo Gil · ORIGAMI Air
gil.summary: Four pours with K-Ultra and Sibarist.
gil.notes: 2024 Dutch champion version. Sibarist model, beans and roast are unspecified. The source suggests about 7 g/s.
gil.s00: Start with a gentle pour of 40 g.
gil.s01: At 0:45 follow up with a pour of 60 g.
gil.s02: At 1:30 continue with a steady pour of 75 g.
gil.s03: At 2:15 conclude with a final pour of 75 g; the card suggests about 7 g/s and drawdown finishing near 3:00.

kasuya.title: Kasuya’s 4:6 method
kasuya.summary: Five pours, clearly timed. The HARIO-published version of Tetsu Kasuya’s 4:6 method.
kasuya.notes: This is HARIO’s published teaching version, not a reconstruction of the competition brew. Its last two pours begin at 2:10 and 2:40.
kasuya.finish: Remove the dripper at the source’s stated finish time.
kasuya.s00: Pour 50 mL at 0:00. The first two pours total 120 mL, or 40% of the water; this first pour is about 41.7% of that first stage and is used to build balance.
kasuya.s01: At 0:45 add 70 mL, supplying the other 58.3% of the first stage and bringing the total to 120 mL.
kasuya.s02: Pour 60 mL at 1:30 — the remaining 180 mL is divided by the source into three equal pours.
kasuya.s03: Pour 60 mL at 2:10, the second of the three equal pours.
kasuya.s04: Begin the final 60 mL at 2:40, reaching 300 mL.

hoffmann.title: A better one-cup V60
hoffmann.summary: A small-batch V60 with measured pours, gentle swirls and short pauses.
hoffmann.notes: Freshly boiled water is the recommendation for lighter roasts. The finish time is approximate; the source prioritizes taste over a fixed drawdown time.
hoffmann.finish: Let the water drain through. Some variation in total time is expected.
hoffmann.s00: Pour 50 g of water to bloom.
hoffmann.s02: Pour up to 100 g total between 0:45 and 1:00 — 40% of the total weight.
hoffmann.s04: Pour up to 150 g total between 1:10 and 1:20 — 60% of the total weight.
hoffmann.s06: Pour up to 200 g total between 1:30 and 1:40 — 80% of the total weight.
hoffmann.s08: Pour up to 250 g total between 1:50 and 2:00 — the full weight.
hoffmann.s09: Gently swirl again for five seconds.

rao.title: Pulsar starting recipe
rao.summary: Valve-controlled blooming and short pulse pours for the NextLevel Pulsar.
rao.grind: Coarser than hand pour, finer than batch brew
rao.notes: The source outline gives a 45–60 second bloom, while its detailed technique resumes at 45–50 seconds. Both are retained here. Pulse amounts and exact later times are not specified.
rao.finish: The target total brew time is a range. Finish draining within that range as described by the source.
rao.s00: With the valve open, pour 75 g of water just off the boil.
rao.s01: Close the valve immediately so the grounds stay submerged.
rao.s02: At 45–50 seconds, pour enough water to raise the slurry about 1 cm above the grounds.
rao.s04: Pour in several short bursts, keeping the slurry 1–2 cm above the grounds, to the 425 g total.
rao.s05: Swirl the Pulsar gently immediately after the last pour.

licata.title: Continuous-pour V60
licata.summary: A forceful start, a slower centre pour, and a turbulent final addition.
licata.notes: Uses light-roasted Colombia La Palma y El Tucan natural Gesha. The intermediate 250 mL total is calculated by subtracting the final 50 mL from the total. Intermediate phase times and the exact point for changing from the forceful pour to the slower centre pour are unspecified; use the source video’s visible flow as the cue.
licata.bloom: Wet the grounds and bloom for 30 seconds.
licata.continuous: Start with a fast, forceful pour, then slow to a centre pour until the cumulative target of 250 mL.
licata.finalPour: Add the final 50 mL quickly to create turbulence.
licata.beans: Light-roasted Colombia La Palma y El Tucan natural Gesha
licata.water: Its unit and reporting basis are not stated.

wong.title: Switch steep and release
wong.summary: Begin with open-valve percolation, then steep and release.
wong.notes: The source says hot water without a temperature or composition. The second addition of 110 g is calculated from the 140 g total minus the 30 g bloom.
wong.finish: At 4:00, close the valve and remove the dripper.
wong.s01: With the valve open, bloom with 30 g of water from 0:00 to 0:10.
wong.s02: Pour to 140 g total between 0:40 and 0:55; the 110 g addition is that target minus the 30 g bloom.
wong.s04: At 1:15 close the valve and pour to 240 g; the 100 g addition is the remaining water.

boen.title: Two-stage Switch immersion
boen.summary: Two closed-valve steeps combined with open-valve percolation.
boen.notes: HARIO’s published 2021 World Brewers Cup recipe. The overview specifies 240 mL, while the steps use g. This discrepancy is preserved without equating the units.
boen.finish: Drain after opening the valve; target a total of 3:00–3:15.
boen.open: Open at 0:40 and immediately start the next pour.
boen.centre: Pour the stated amount into the centre.
boen.circle: Add the stated amount in a circular pattern.
boen.beans: Natural Geisha from Hacienda La Esmeralda
boen.s01: With the dripper closed, pour 50 g of water for the bloom and leave it for 40 seconds.

hoang.title: Dual-filter W60
hoang.summary: A flat mesh bed and paper filter with three water additions.
hoang.notes: HARIO’s published 2021 World Brewers Cup recipe. The overview gives 200 g, but the steps use mL. Both are preserved without assuming equivalence. The card does not describe how to seat the paper on the W60 metal mesh; follow the manufacturer’s assembly instructions before brewing.
hoang.water: It is not stated whether the figure is hardness or total dissolved solids.
hoang.filters: W60 flat mesh and paper filter used together.
hoang.prep: The author recommends sifting out fines before brewing.
hoang.s00: Bloom with 50 mL of water for 30 seconds.
hoang.s01: Pour another 100 mL of water over 30 seconds.
hoang.s02: Pour the final 50 mL of water at 2:00.

rojewska.title: Fast two-stage V60
rojewska.summary: Gentle circular pouring followed by a fast centre pour.
rojewska.notes: The listed 1:00 is the end of pouring; the total target is 2:15. Bloom amount and temperature are unspecified. The 150 mL is a cumulative target, not a post-bloom addition.
rojewska.finish: Stop pouring around 1:00 and let drain; target a total of 2:15.
rojewska.bloom: Pre-infuse for 15 seconds; the water amount is unspecified.
rojewska.circle: Pour gently in circles to a cumulative 150 mL, including the pre-infusion water.
rojewska.centre: Add the remaining 100 mL quickly in the centre, maintaining the water level; stop around 1:00.

grill.title: Martha Grill’s morning V60
grill.summary: A 30 g V60 with a 30-second bloom, two pours and a finish at three minutes.
grill.notes: The published recipe uses 30 g coffee and 500 mL at 92 °C. Its pour targets are written in g, so those units remain separate rather than being converted. The article names Ézio Sartori coffee from Brazil but does not name a grind setting.
grill.beans: Ézio Sartori, Espírito Santo, Brazil; roasted by Coffee Lab
grill.s00: Pour 60 g of water and let it bloom for 30 seconds.
grill.s01: On the second pour go to 250 g; the 190 g addition is that target minus the bloom.
grill.s02: After the pour reaches 250 g, stir three times.
grill.s03: At 1:30 pour the rest of the water, taking the total to 500 g.
grill.s04: After the 1:30 pour finishes, stir three times again.
grill.taste1: About the coffee she brews here: floral aroma, a bright acidity.

mallouhi.title: Ibrahim Al Mallouhi’s V60
mallouhi.summary: A 1:15 V60 with a 40 mL circular bloom and a slow remaining pour.
mallouhi.notes: The source states 20 g coffee, 300 mL water and a 2:10 target, but does not specify water temperature.
mallouhi.finish: Target a total brew time of 2:10.
mallouhi.prep: Pre-wet the filter and discard the rinse water before adding coffee.
mallouhi.water: The source says hot water but does not provide a temperature.
mallouhi.s00: Slowly pour 40 mL of hot water in circular motions, then let it bloom for 35 seconds.
mallouhi.s01: Slowly pour the remaining water — 260 mL, the published 300 mL less the bloom — in small circular motions.

chronicler.title: Coffee Chronicler Switch recipe
chronicler.summary: A two-pour Switch recipe: half the water open, half steeped, then released.
chronicler.notes: The article’s standard version uses 20 g coffee and 320 mL water: pour half with the valve open, close at 0:45, add the remaining half, then open at 2:00. Temperature and grind are not specified.
chronicler.finish: Let the brew drain; the article gives a 2:45–3:15 total range.
chronicler.open: Start with the Switch valve open.
chronicler.firstPour: Pour the first half of the water while the valve is open.
chronicler.close: Close the valve at 0:45 for the steep.
chronicler.secondPour: Add the remaining half of the water, then steep.
chronicler.drain: Open at 2:00 and let the brew drain.

hoffmann-ultimate.title: The ultimate V60 technique
hoffmann-ultimate.summary: A 30 g V60 recipe with a 60 g bloom, staged pours to 500 g and a final stir.
hoffmann-ultimate.notes: The source recommends water as hot as possible, especially for lighter roasts. The finish time is a target; drawdown varies with paper and temperature.
hoffmann-ultimate.finish: Let the brew draw down, aiming to finish around 3:30.
hoffmann-ultimate.s00: At t = 0:00 add twice the coffee weight, 60 g of bloom water.
hoffmann-ultimate.s01: Swirl the slurry until evenly mixed so all grounds are wetted — the source prefers swirling to a spoon here.
hoffmann-ultimate.s02: Bloom for up to 45 seconds, then add 240 g over the next 30 seconds to reach 300 g, 60% of the total brew weight.
hoffmann-ultimate.s03: Add the last 200 g over 30 seconds to reach 500 g, a little slower than the previous phase and not too aggressively.
hoffmann-ultimate.s04: At t = 1:45 stir once clockwise with a spoon.
hoffmann-ultimate.s05: Then stir once anticlockwise with the spoon.
hoffmann-ultimate.s06: Allow the V60 to drain a little.
hoffmann-ultimate.s07: Give the V60 a gentle swirl, then let it draw down — the source aims to finish by 3:30.

camber.title: Camber Coffee V60
camber.summary: A 20 g V60 recipe with a 60 g bloom and two pours to 345 g, shared for anaerobic coffees.
camber.notes: The source recommends this recipe for anaerobic processed coffees. Water temperature is not stated.
camber.finish: Aim for a total brew time of 3:00–3:15.
camber.bean: The source recommends anaerobic processed coffees.
camber.s00: Bloom with 60 g of water between 0:00 and 0:30.
camber.s01: Pour up to 200 g between 0:30 and 0:45.
camber.s02: At 1:00 make the final pour up to 345 g.

lamill.title: LAMILL V60 Mugen
lamill.summary: A 16.5 g one-pour Mugen recipe with 225 g water and a 3:00–3:30 drawdown.
lamill.notes: The source uses no bloom or temperature specification; it asks for one continuous concentric pour finishing at 0:40.
lamill.finish: Allow the bed to draw down, aiming for 3:00–3:30.
lamill.prepare: Pre-wet the filter, add 16.5 g of coffee and make a small crater in the centre.
lamill.s00: Start the timer and pour all 225 g in concentric circles from the centre slowly outward, finishing this single pour at 0:40.

medina.title: Medina’s 30-second pulse pours
medina.summary: 15.5 g of coffee at 91 °C, with 50 g added every 30 seconds, five times in all.
medina.equipment: No dripper stated; the card is filed only under “Pour-over”
medina.notes: The card publishes only 15.5 g of coffee, 250 g of water at 91 °C, and 50 g every 30 seconds. Dripper, filter, total time and pour path are absent, so the five additions and their clock times are calculated from that interval and total.
medina.finish: No finish time is published; drawdown is left to the brewer.
medina.overview: Dividing the water into identical shares on a fixed interval gives one of the easiest structures to follow with a timer. With dose and temperature settled, the only variable left is your own pouring rhythm.
medina.bestFor: Anyone who wants a fixed-interval, equal-share pour
medina.s00: Add 50 g — the first of five equal additions on a 30-second interval.
medina.s04: Pour the last 50 g at 2:00, reaching the 250 g total.

maisonnette.title: Maisonnette’s two-grind layered brew
maisonnette.summary: Two coffees ground separately at 7.5 and 7.0, layered, then four timed pours to 240 g.
maisonnette.notes: 12 g Obatã at 7.5 and 4 g Catucaí 24/137 at 7.0 are ground separately and stacked Obatã-first; the bottom of the glass server is chilled to −10 °C before extraction. No total brew time is published.
maisonnette.finish: No total time is published; the last pour window closes at 2:30.
maisonnette.overview: Grinding two coffees to two settings within one brew trades prep steps for flavour separation; the chilled server base carries the same idea into the liquid, dropping the first drips in temperature straight away.
maisonnette.bestFor: Brewers happy to prep harder to compare two grinds
maisonnette.prepare: Grind 12 g of Obatã at 7.5 for the bottom layer and 4 g of Catucaí at 7.0 for the top layer. Chill the glass server base to −10 °C before brewing.
maisonnette.s00: Pour 60 g between 0:00 and 0:35 and let it bloom.
maisonnette.s03: Pour the final 50 g between 1:40 and 2:30.

torres.title: Torres’ three equal circular pours
torres.summary: 17 g to 240 g in three 80 g pours, with about two minutes in mind.
torres.notes: The card names 17 g of “bourbon striped, farm paradise 92” and three 80 g pours at 0:00, 0:40 and 1:20. Dripper, filter and pouring height are not given.
torres.finish: Let it drain fully; the source puts the whole brew at about 2:00.
torres.overview: Repeating the same 80 g three times, with a circle and a slower flow added only from the second pour, compresses the recipe down to the pouring path itself.
torres.bestFor: Brewers who want to tune flavour through the pour path alone
torres.s00: Start the timer and pour 80 g evenly over the grounds, then let it bloom.
torres.s01: At 0:40 add another 80 g in slow, circular motions.
torres.s02: At 1:20 pour the final 80 g, again in circles.

pinnola.title: Pinnola’s three cumulative pours on a Graycano
pinnola.summary: 15 g of washed Geisha from Finca Rosario: a 40 g bloom, then top-ups to 140 g and 240 g.
pinnola.notes: The second and third pours are published as cumulative targets, so both 100 g additions come from 140 − 40 and 240 − 140. The paper is only “Sibarist”, with no model, and no stage times or temperatures are given.
pinnola.finish: No end time is published; after 240 g, let it drain.
pinnola.overview: Writing the pours as cumulative totals means you only chase two numbers on the scale. It is a competition recipe for a light-roast Geisha that trades agitation for aroma.
pinnola.bestFor: Brewers who want to chase two numbers on the scale
pinnola.s00: Add 40 g of water and let it bloom.
pinnola.s01: Pour up to 140 g in a controlled, circular motion.
pinnola.s02: Pour up to 240 g to complete the brew.

kaygusuz.title: Kaygusuz’s four pours and mixed water
kaygusuz.summary: A 12 g + 5 g blend on 72 ppm self-mixed water, four pours to 270 g, finished at 2:40.
kaygusuz.equipment: Graycano with Sibarist paper and a Melodrip
kaygusuz.water: Apax water mixed to 72 ppm from Tonik 1 g, Jamm 1.5 g and Lylac 1.5 g; the water volume those powders dissolve into is not stated.
kaygusuz.notes: The source gives a 40-second bloom, then waits until 1:20 before the third pour and 2:00 before the fourth. It gives no separate start time for the second 60 g pour, so that addition remains a sequence step.
kaygusuz.finish: The source states a total brew time of 2:40.
kaygusuz.overview: Self-mixed water, a two-farm blend and a Melodrip put every variable under the brewer’s control, while the pouring schedule itself stays deliberately plain.
kaygusuz.bestFor: Brewers who mix their own water and want variables isolated
kaygusuz.s00: Add 60 g of water and let it bloom for 40 seconds.
kaygusuz.s03: Wait until 2:00, then pour the final 100 g.

vuolo.title: Vuolo’s two quick circles and a centre finish
vuolo.summary: A 15 g blend takes two 100 g circular pours at 96 °C, then 40 g at 90 °C poured centrally and continuously.
vuolo.equipment: MK dripper with Sibarist Flat paper
vuolo.notes: The card gives no overall water temperature — only 96 °C for the first two pours and 90 °C for the last — and publishes neither pour times nor a total brew time.
vuolo.finish: No finish time is given; after the three pours, let it drain.
vuolo.overview: Two hot circular pours drive extraction hard, then the last addition drops the temperature and narrows to a centre stream — agitation and heat used as switches.
vuolo.bestFor: Brewers who push extraction early and cool it at the end
vuolo.s00: Pour 100 g at 96 °C in quick circular movements.
vuolo.s01: Repeat the same: 100 g at 96 °C, quick circles.
vuolo.s02: Add the last 40 g at 90 °C as a central, continuous stream.

damgaci.title: Damgacı’s five pours in a ceramic V60
damgaci.summary: Three coffees at 5 g each, a 40 g bloom and four 50 g pours, done at 2:20.
damgaci.water: Reverse-osmosis water at 40 ppm; the mineral composition is not given.
damgaci.notes: Only the 30-second bloom and the 2:20 total are timed; the four later additions have no clock times, so they stay ordered steps.
damgaci.finish: The source states a total brew time of 2:20.
damgaci.overview: Three single origins at 5 g each are blended in the hopper, while the pour stays plain: three circles, then one centre finish. Complexity comes from the beans; consistency comes from the schedule.
damgaci.bestFor: Brewers blending several coffees inside a competition structure
damgaci.s00: Add 40 g of water and let it bloom for 30 seconds.
damgaci.s01: Second pour: 50 g in a circular motion.
damgaci.s02: Third pour: another 50 g in a circle.
damgaci.s03: Fourth pour: the same circular 50 g.
damgaci.s04: Fifth pour: the final 50 g poured to the centre.

ohno.title: Ohno’s cool, coarse brew with a water top-up
ohno.summary: Extract 22 g with 190 g at 83 °C, let it drain in 1:30–1:35, then dilute in the cup with 65 °C water, starting at 50 g and adjusting toward 60–70 g.
ohno.equipment: ORIGAMI Dripper Air S with Wave paper
ohno.water: Tajima natural water, supplied by the event to every competitor; no hardness or TDS basis is stated.
ohno.notes: The 190 g is extraction water only. The dilution starts at 50 g and can rise to about 60–70 g total by taste; that range is not part of the 190 g brew water.
ohno.prepare: Grind 32 g at 30 clicks and sieve it through the coarsest mesh L stocker, then use 22.0 g.
ohno.finish: Stir the diluted coffee and serve.
ohno.overview: The temperature is deliberately low, the grind coarse and the bed flat, so the brew comes out under-extracted and pale on purpose; the finishing water then sets the strength. With clean cup as the judging criterion, the risk is pushed onto the weak side.
ohno.bestFor: Competitors who want to set strength with a finishing water
ohno.s00: First pour of 45 g, spreading the water across the whole bed.
ohno.s01: At 0:30 go to 120 g (+75 g) with a slow circle, aiming at a little agitation.
ohno.s02: At 1:00 go to 190 g (+70 g) with a centre pour that avoids agitation, then circle the wall for the last ~15 g so the bed finishes flat.
ohno.s03: Let the 190 g brew drain completely. The source puts drop-off at 1:30–1:35; this ends extraction before dilution.
ohno.beans: Ohno notes that the bean profile was only released on the day, so his card is written to suit any coffee and names no bean.
ohno.taste1: His stated goal is a clean cup and sweetness, and the low temperature and coarse sieve are chosen for it.
ohno.taste2: The coffee served measured TDS 1.07 — deliberately dilute, closer to tea in strength.
ohno.quickAnswer: Quick answer: 22 g at {temperature}, 190 g across three pours, draining at 1:30–1:35. Then dilute in the cup with 65 °C water: start at 50 g and adjust toward 60–70 g.
ohno.s04: Add 65 °C water to the brewed coffee. Start with 50 g, taste, and raise the total finishing water toward 60–70 g.

gil-2025.title: Gil’s 2025 three-pour ZP6 recipe
gil-2025.summary: 15 g to 250 g of 65 ppm water at 94 °C, in 60, 100 and 90 g pours spaced 50 seconds apart.
gil-2025.equipment: The card says only “place in the dripper”, naming neither dripper nor filter
gil-2025.water: 65 ppm water; neither its composition nor its reporting basis is stated.
gil-2025.notes: This is Gil’s 2025 ZP6 version, kept separate from his 2024 K-Ultra and ORIGAMI Air recipe; no total brew time is published.
gil-2025.finish: No finish time is given; after the three pours, let it drain.
gil-2025.overview: The same author changed grinder and structure a year later: three larger pours. The intervals are 50 seconds in this 2025 version versus 45 seconds in 2024, while the card says this cup stays clean and expressive.
gil-2025.bestFor: Comparing two versions by the same brewer a year apart
gil-2025.s00: Place 15 g of coffee in the dripper and open with a 60 g pour.
gil-2025.s02: After another 50 seconds, pour the final 90 g.

kurasu.title: Kurasu’s flash-brew iced filter
kurasu.summary: Fifteen grams to 150 g of hot water poured over 65–70 g of ice, in three additions finishing around 1:45.
kurasu.grind: Finer than a standard hot pour-over
kurasu.equipment: Dripper and filter not named; the paper is rinsed and the dripper warmed
kurasu.notes: The page names neither the dripper nor a water temperature; it was published on 2026-09-23. Ice is published as approximately 65–70 g and described as what sets the final strength; stir until it has fully melted before serving.
kurasu.finish: Aim to finish around 1:40–1:45, then remove the dripper and stir until the remaining ice has melted.
kurasu.overview: Flash brewing runs a concentrated hot brew straight onto ice, so cooling and dilution happen together and the ice weight becomes the strength dial — the point the page stresses most. Temperature is left unstated, which leaves that one lever to taste.
kurasu.bestFor: Light-roast filter coffee you want cold without a twelve-hour wait
kurasu.prepare: Rinse the paper filter, warm the dripper, then put approximately 65–70 g of ice in the server.
kurasu.s00: Pour 40 g of water for the bloom.
kurasu.s01: At 0:40, pour to 100 g in total.
kurasu.s02: At 1:10, pour gently and slowly to 150 g in total, avoiding excessive agitation.
kurasu.taste1: The page states the ice weight directly affects the final strength, which makes it the dial for how strong the cup lands.
kurasu.taste2: With the Kenya Kangocho AA on the page, the method brings forward juicy berry sweetness and a grape-like acidity.

ona-iris.title: Iris Estate Enigma · Espresso
ona-iris.summary: ONA's lot guide for Iris Estate Enigma: 20.3 g in, 44 g out in 24 seconds at 93.5 °C, brewed 10–25 days after roast.
ona-iris.notes: The source presents these numbers as a starting range, not a fixed rule. It also gives a best-freeze window of 10–14 days after roast and describes the cup as blackberry, chocolate and cherry.
ona-iris.overview: A single-lot espresso guide from ONA's brew-guide library, written for the Iris Estate Enigma CM Natural.
ona-iris.bestFor: Anyone brewing this ONA lot who wants the roaster's own starting recipe.
ona-iris.beanNote: CM Natural is the source's own process label; it also asks for 10–25 days of rest after roast.

camber-espresso.title: Camber Espresso Recipe
camber-espresso.summary: Camber's café baseline: 19 g in, 38 g out in 25–30 seconds at 202–204 °F, a 1:2 recipe.
camber-espresso.grind: Fine enough that the shot runs 25–30 seconds; the source gives no grinder setting
camber-espresso.notes: The source presents this as a starting recipe for dialling in, and notes that water flows through the least dense parts of the puck, so a level tamp matters.
camber-espresso.s00: Grind for espresso and use a 25–30 second shot as the adjustment target.
camber-espresso.s02: Distribute the coffee until the bed is level.
camber-espresso.s03: Tamp level. Even distribution and a level bed matter because water follows paths of least resistance.
camber-espresso.s04: Start timing when the machine engages. At 202–204 °F, extract 38 g over about 25–30 seconds.
camber-espresso.s05: Stop at 38 g, then use the actual time to adjust grind.
camber-espresso.teach1: Grind is the main control for shot time: finer grinds slow the flow and increase extraction.
camber-espresso.teach2: Water takes the least-resistant route through the puck, so density differences can extract one part more than another.
camber-espresso.teach3: Shot time means from engaging the machine until the desired yield is reached.
camber-espresso.overview: A roastery's written espresso baseline, kept in Fahrenheit exactly as published.
camber-espresso.bestFor: Home brewers who want a documented starting point before adjusting to taste.

counterculture-go-to.title: Counter Culture Go-To Espresso
counterculture-go-to.summary: Counter Culture's baseline recipe: 18 g in, 36 g out, 28 seconds.
counterculture-go-to.notes: The source calls this a baseline for dialling in an unfamiliar coffee, not a claim about every bean.
counterculture-go-to.overview: A widely used café baseline from Counter Culture's espresso guide.
counterculture-go-to.bestFor: A first reference point when a new coffee has no published recipe.

rolf-v60.title: April’s 13 g V60 in four pours
rolf-v60.summary: Thirteen grams to 200 g at 90 °C, four equal 50 g pours 30 seconds apart, done at 2:30.
rolf-v60.equipment: HARIO V60 02; the paper brand is not named
rolf-v60.notes: The written description fixes the dose, water, temperature, four pour times and finish. The video adds a 30-click Comandante setting, a rinsed paper and a swirl/tap after the final pour; Rolf says 90 °C is chosen for acidity and vibrancy. Coffee and paper brand remain unstated.
rolf-v60.finish: The written source gives 2:30 as the total brew time. In the video Rolf lifts the brewer at about 2:30 after it has drained, then swirls and lets it rest briefly.
rolf-v60.overview: Four identical 50 g pours leave grind as the only variable. Rolf keeps the dose at 13 g, which makes a shallow bed, so the relatively coarse grind is what keeps the flow even.
rolf-v60.bestFor: A small, repeatable V60 you can time one-handed
rolf-v60.s00: Pour 50 g for the bloom at 0:00.
rolf-v60.s03: At 1:30 pour the last 50 g, reaching 200 g.
rolf-v60.teach1: The coarse grind is deliberate: a 13 g bed is shallow, and a finer grind would stall it.
rolf-v60.teach2: Every pour is the same 50 g at the same 30-second spacing — no ramp, no pulses.
rolf-v60.teach3: 2:30 is the source’s total brew time, not a drawdown deadline.

rolf-origami.title: April’s Origami with a V60 paper
rolf-origami.summary: Twenty grams to 300 g at 92 °C: a 100 g circle, then 200 g poured continuously from 0:45 to 1:20.
rolf-origami.equipment: ORIGAMI Dripper with a cone-shaped V60 02 paper
rolf-origami.notes: The video deliberately pairs the Origami dripper with a cone V60 02 paper rather than Origami’s own wave filter. The spoken Comandante setting is about 29–30 clicks, a little finer than their usual setting to offset the faster flow. Rolf also warns that roast degree changes bed resistance.
rolf-origami.finish: The written source gives 2:30 as total brew time; the spoken demonstration describes approximately 2:30–2:40.
rolf-origami.overview: Two pours only: a quick 100 g circle opens the bed, then 35 seconds of continuous pouring keeps it moving. The cone paper in a flat-bed dripper flows slower than a wave filter, which is the interesting part.
rolf-origami.bestFor: Anyone with an Origami and only V60 papers
rolf-origami.s01: From 0:45 to 1:20 pour 200 g continuously in circles, reaching 300 g.
rolf-origami.teach1: The second pour is continuous, not pulsed: 200 g across 35 seconds keeps the bed moving.
rolf-origami.teach2: Roast changes bed resistance: with a darker coffee than theirs, grind slightly finer to keep the 2:30.

kasuya-neo.title: Kasuya’s NEO: ten pours of 30 grams
kasuya-neo.summary: Twenty grams to 300 g at 95–96 °C, extra coarse: first pour at 0:00, wait 30 seconds, then nine more 30 g pours 15 seconds apart.
kasuya-neo.equipment: HARIO NEO; the source says a V60 also works
kasuya-neo.notes: The description gives no total brew time. In the video the final pour starts at 2:30 and Kasuya expects draining around 3:30, but the editable duration stays unset because that timing is video narration rather than a fixed text-layer value. A V60 is also acceptable.
kasuya-neo.finish: No finish time is published; the only requirement is that the water never sits in the dripper.
kasuya-neo.overview: A deliberate counterpoint to the short, low-pour trend: extra-coarse and hot, then ten small additions build sweetness and texture. The counter-intuitive part is the grind — 40–45 clicks, taking extraction from rhythm rather than fines.
kasuya-neo.bestFor: Brewers practising pour rhythm rather than pour volume
kasuya-neo.s00: Pour the first 30 g at 0:00, letting it pass through rather than pool. Wait 30 seconds before the second pour.
kasuya-neo.pour: Pour another 30 g, 15 seconds after the previous pour.
kasuya-neo.s09: At 2:30 make the tenth and final 30 g pour, reaching 300 g.
kasuya-neo.teach1: Extra-coarse grind plus 95–96 °C is the counter-intuitive pair the whole recipe rests on.
kasuya-neo.teach2: Ten additions of 30 g every 15 seconds; the point is that the water passes through the bed rather than sitting on it.
kasuya-neo.teach3: Kasuya recommends the NEO because it extracts small additions evenly, but says a V60 is equally acceptable.
kasuya-neo.taste1: Kasuya’s own claim: extra-coarse grind with 95–96 °C and ten small pours builds sweetness.
kasuya-neo.taste2: He credits the ten pours, not fines, for the body: a syrupy mouthfeel he calls とろみ.
kasuya-neo.taste3: Kasuya says the sweetness dominates and acidity is softened; 45 clicks can be thin, while 40 clicks is much easier to repeat.

kasuya-iced.title: Kasuya’s iced 4:6
kasuya-iced.summary: Twenty grams with 150 g of hot water in five 30 g additions, brewed through the dripper into a server holding 80 g of ice. Temperature is 90–93 °C.
kasuya-iced.equipment: A regular dripper; the source never names it
kasuya-iced.notes: These parameters are shared by both recipes compared in the video — the 4:6 over ice and a Switch hybrid. Water is half the usual 300 g because 80 g of ice already sits in the server. No pour times and no total time are published for this version.
kasuya-iced.finish: No finish time is published; let it drain fully over the ice.
kasuya-iced.overview: The 4:6 idea scaled down for ice: half the water, five equal pours, and the ice in the server doing the chilling and the diluting. With nothing timed beyond the pour count, it is a shape to follow rather than a schedule.
kasuya-iced.bestFor: A 4:6 habit applied to ice, without buying a Switch
kasuya-iced.s00: Put 80 g of ice in the server. Pour the first 30 g of hot water over the coffee bed; the brewed liquid then drips onto the ice.
kasuya-iced.pour: Another 30 g, keeping to five pours in total.
kasuya-iced.s04: The fifth and final 30 g, reaching 150 g.
kasuya-iced.teach1: Water drops to 150 g — half the normal 4:6 — because 80 g of ice is already in the server.
kasuya-iced.teach2: Five pours of 30 g in total; the video gives no times, so the count is the instruction.
kasuya-iced.teach3: 90–93 °C is the temperature range shared by both iced versions in the video.
kasuya-iced.taste3: In the comparison Kasuya prefers the Switch hybrid for its smoother, sweeter cup; the 4:6 application keeps more brightness.

woelfl.title: Wölfl’s V60 with a 60 g bloom
woelfl.summary: Twenty grams to 300 ml at 93 °C: a 60 ml bloom for 30–40 seconds, then the remaining 240 ml, in 2:30–3:00.
woelfl.equipment: HARIO V60; the paper brand is not named
woelfl.notes: The description gives the bloom volume and the total time but no time for the second pour, so it stays untimed. Grinder, coffee and paper brand are not named.
woelfl.finish: The whole brew should take about 2:30–3:00 by the source.
woelfl.overview: A teaching recipe that explains itself: rinsing the paper and carafe warms them and keeps paper taste out, the 30–40 second bloom lets CO₂ escape, and the last 240 ml goes in slowly and steadily.
woelfl.bestFor: Learning the bloom-and-one-pour structure together with the reasons
woelfl.s00: Pour about 60 ml in circles and let it bloom for 30–40 seconds.
woelfl.s01: Pour the remaining 240 ml slowly and steadily, in circles or through the centre.
woelfl.teach1: Rinse the paper and the carafe with hot water: it warms both and keeps paper taste out of the cup.
woelfl.teach2: Bloom for 30–40 seconds; the source suggests smelling the bed up close to follow the degassing.
woelfl.teach3: The second pour is the remaining 240 ml, slow and steady rather than in pulses.
woelfl.teach4: Swirl the carafe well or stir with a spoon before drinking so the layers mix.

lamarzocco.title: La Marzocco's basic espresso recipe
lamarzocco.summary: La Marzocco's starting recipe: 18 g in, 36 g out in 25–35 seconds at 93 °C and 9 bar, using a 17 g basket and a medium roast blend.
lamarzocco.grind: Not stated by the source; adjust the grind to reach 36 g in 25–35 seconds
lamarzocco.notes: The article gives three priorities: a medium roast espresso blend, a 1:2 ratio and the time window. Its worked example is 18 g → 36 g in 30 seconds; 93 °C and 9 bar are the factory settings it recommends holding.
lamarzocco.overview: A written baseline from La Marzocco's home education series, built around the Linea Micra's factory temperature and pressure.
lamarzocco.bestFor: Home brewers who want a repeatable 1:2 starting point on a La Marzocco machine.
lamarzocco.s00: Put 18 g of ground coffee into the 17 g basket, using a scale.
lamarzocco.s01: Start the shot at 93 °C and 9 bar. Aim for 36 g of espresso in 25–35 seconds; the source's worked example is 30 seconds.
lamarzocco.teach1: The source's first priority is a medium roast espresso blend: rich brown, without visible oil on the beans.
lamarzocco.teach2: It treats 18 g → 36 g as a normale 1:2 ratio; 30 seconds is the example inside the 25–35 second window.
lamarzocco.teach3: Once you find a coffee you like, keep using it long enough to repeat the recipe and learn its best taste.

coffeecollective.title: Coffee Collective's espresso guide
coffeecollective.summary: Coffee Collective's café baseline: 19 g in, 38 g out in 27 seconds at 93 °C and 7 bar, using an 18 g or 20 g VST basket.
coffeecollective.grind: Very fine; adjust the grind so the full 38 g arrives in about 27 seconds
coffeecollective.notes: The guide pairs a 1:2 ratio with a 7 bar brew pressure and a VST basket. It asks for a level 10–15 kg tamp and a quick stir before drinking; no coffee, grinder or roast is named.
coffeecollective.water: The source states water quality below 50 ppm CaCO₃; it does not translate this into a general hardness or alkalinity target.
coffeecollective.overview: A concise espresso guide from a Copenhagen roastery, built around a 19 g double, a 27-second shot and a VST basket.
coffeecollective.bestFor: Home brewers using a VST basket who want a clean, Nordic-style 1:2 recipe.
coffeecollective.s00: Weigh 19 g of coffee for a double espresso.
coffeecollective.s01: Distribute the grounds evenly until the bed in the basket is flat.
coffeecollective.s02: Tamp level with 10–15 kg of pressure; the source says level matters more than force.
coffeecollective.s03: Brew at 93 °C and 7 bar. Adjust the grind so the full 38 g arrives in about 27 seconds.
coffeecollective.s04: Stop at 38 g, then stir the espresso briefly before drinking to mix the layers.
coffeecollective.teach1: The grind is the adjustment: keep the dose and yield fixed, and change the grind until the shot reaches 27 seconds.
coffeecollective.teach2: A level tamp with 10–15 kg is the source's only puck-prep instruction; it stresses level over pressure.
coffeecollective.teach3: A quick stir before drinking is part of the recipe, not just presentation: it mixes the layers for a more balanced cup.

onyx-monarch.title: Monarch · Espresso
onyx-monarch.summary: Onyx’s Monarch espresso card: 19 g in, 47 g out, 3.5 seconds of line pressure before 9 bar. It labels “9 Bar: 23s”, without saying what that 23 seconds includes.
onyx-monarch.grind: Not stated by the espresso card
onyx-monarch.notes: Monarch is a washed Colombia–Ethiopia blend roasted Expressive Dark and designed for milk. The card links a Fellow Series 1 profile and lists line pressure for 0–3.5 s, then “9 Bar: 23s”; the basis of 23 seconds remains unknown, and no brew temperature, basket or grinder is stated.
onyx-monarch.overview: Onyx's espresso guide pairs a dark, milk-friendly blend with a short line-pressure pre-infusion and a 9 bar finish.
onyx-monarch.bestFor: Anyone brewing Monarch who wants Onyx's own espresso-facing starting point.
onyx-monarch.s00: Start with line pressure for the first 3.5 seconds; the source does not state the pre-infusion pressure.
onyx-monarch.s01: Raise to 9 bar and extract to 47 g. The source labels the stage 23 seconds, but does not say whether that includes the 3.5-second line-pressure phase.
onyx-monarch.s02: Stop when the yield reaches 47 g. Treat 23 seconds as a source label whose timing basis is unresolved.
onyx-monarch.teach1: The espresso card links a Fellow Series 1 profile for this coffee.
onyx-monarch.teach2: The linked Series 1 profile calls Monarch a blend designed to work with milk.
onyx-monarch.tasting: Dark chocolate, molasses, red wine and dried berries; thick and syrupy.

onyx-aponte.title: Aponte Village · Espresso
onyx-aponte.summary: Onyx’s Aponte Village espresso card: 20 g in, 48 g out, 3.5 seconds of line pressure before 9 bar. It labels “9 Bar: 24s”, without saying what that 24 seconds includes.
onyx-aponte.grind: Not stated by the espresso card
onyx-aponte.notes: Aponte Village is a Red Honey Colombia coffee roasted light. The card lists line pressure for 0–3.5 s, then “9 Bar: 24s”; the basis of 24 seconds remains unknown, and no brew temperature, basket or grinder is stated.
onyx-aponte.overview: A light, honey-processed Colombian espresso built on Onyx's line-pressure profile for a 20 g dose.
onyx-aponte.bestFor: Brewers who want a light, honey-processed espresso with a long 1:2.4 yield.
onyx-aponte.s00: Start with line pressure for the first 3.5 seconds; the source does not state the pre-infusion pressure.
onyx-aponte.s01: Raise to 9 bar and extract to 48 g. The source labels the stage 24 seconds, but does not say whether that includes the 3.5-second line-pressure phase.
onyx-aponte.s02: Stop when the yield reaches 48 g. Treat 24 seconds as a source label whose timing basis is unresolved.
onyx-aponte.teach1: Red Honey is Onyx's own process label for this coffee.
onyx-aponte.teach2: The card gives no brew temperature, grinder or basket, so those values remain open.
onyx-aponte.tasting: Honeycrisp apple, cherry, vanilla and papaya.

hedrick-ultimate.title: Lance Hedrick’s flexible pour-over framework
hedrick-ultimate.summary: Up to 30 g at a 1:14–1:17 ratio and 85–100 °C, with a 3× bloom and a roast-dependent finish in roughly 2–4 minutes.
hedrick-ultimate.equipment: Any pour-over brewer; the source does not name one
hedrick-ultimate.notes: The 30 g value is the source’s ceiling, not a required dose. Choose a dose, calculate water with 1:14–1:17, and make the bloom three times that dose. The video uses 15 g and 255 g water as a concrete demonstration; the 420–510 g range belongs only to the 30 g maximum.
hedrick-ultimate.finish: The source gives 2–3 minutes after a 1-minute bloom, or 3–4 minutes after a 2-minute bloom.
hedrick-ultimate.overview: A deliberately adjustable framework rather than a single recipe. Roast level moves the ratio and temperature, while the pour rate, bloom and bed agitation stay fixed enough to repeat.
hedrick-ultimate.bestFor: Brewers who want one structured method they can tune across roast levels
hedrick-ultimate.s00: Bloom with three times the dose you chose.
hedrick-ultimate.pour: Pour the remaining water at 6–8 g/s from a height that creates deep turbulence; the chosen ratio sets how much remains.
hedrick-ultimate.teach1: Use up to 30 g; the recipe scales around that ceiling rather than prescribing 30 g every time.
hedrick-ultimate.teach2: Roast level moves the ratio between 1:14 and 1:17 and the temperature between 85 and 100 °C; the source does not prescribe one fixed pairing.
hedrick-ultimate.teach3: Agitate the bloom, then wait 1–2 minutes before the main pour.
hedrick-ultimate.teach4: The remaining water goes in at 6–8 g/s with enough height for deep turbulence.
hedrick-ultimate.teach5: Choose the finishing action by flow: swirl if slow, use Wet WDT if somewhat quick, or turn the bed over with a spoon if fast.
hedrick-ultimate.taste1: Hedrick reports roughly 20–21% extraction across his test of the framework.
hedrick-ultimate.taste2: He describes low bitterness and no astringent finish from the coarse grind and relatively fast brew.
hedrick-ultimate.taste3: His tasting language is citric acidity, sweetness, and a velvety, pillowy body.
hedrick-ultimate.quickAnswer: Quick answer: choose any dose up to 30 g; set water to 1:14–1:17, bloom with 3× the dose, then pour the rest at 6–8 g/s. Use {temperature} by roast. Total time is 2–3 minutes with a 1-minute bloom or 3–4 minutes with a 2-minute bloom.
hedrick-ultimate.agitate: Agitate the bloom so every ground is wet; the source permits excavating the bed or using Wet WDT.
hedrick-ultimate.wait: Wait 1–2 minutes, depending on the coffee and roast, before the main pour.

chronicler-osmotic.title: Coffee Chronicler’s osmotic-flow V60
chronicler-osmotic.summary: 14–20 g at 1:15 and 93 °C, medium-coarse, with a 40-second 2.5× bloom and a 3–5 minute brew.
chronicler-osmotic.equipment: HARIO V60 with a Cafec T90 paper filter
chronicler-osmotic.notes: The description says a 40-second bloom; the video narration says 45 seconds. This page keeps 40 seconds because it is the author-written numeric layer and records the discrepancy separately. The 210–300 ml water range is derived from the stated 1:15 ratio; later pours have no exact times.
chronicler-osmotic.water: The video recommends soft water with TDS 50–110 ppm; no fuller mineral profile is stated.
chronicler-osmotic.finish: The source gives about 3–5 minutes total.
chronicler-osmotic.overview: A centre-first V60 routine built around osmotic flow: a measured bloom, a gentle centre pour to half the brew volume, then a slowly expanding circle for the rest.
chronicler-osmotic.bestFor: A low-effort V60 method with a clear centre-first pour
chronicler-osmotic.s00: Bloom for 40 seconds with 2.5× the dry dose: 35–50 ml across the 14–20 g range.
chronicler-osmotic.s01: After the bloom, gently pour in the centre until the brew reaches 50% of its total volume.
chronicler-osmotic.s02: Pour the rest in a slowly expanding circle, keeping the water off the paper filter.
chronicler-osmotic.teach1: Choose any dose from 14–20 g and keep the water at 1:15; the 210–300 ml totals in the recipe-card header are that range.
chronicler-osmotic.teach2: The first full pour goes down the centre, not around the wall of the dripper.
chronicler-osmotic.teach3: Only the final pour expands in circles; the source explicitly says to avoid pouring on the paper.
chronicler-osmotic.teach4: Use soft water, preferably below 110 ppm, a bleached Cafec cone filter, and keep the kettle low to minimise agitation.
chronicler-osmotic.teach5: Never pour on the paper and do not pour faster than the bed drains; a wet-sand bed without surface silt is the visual cue.
chronicler-osmotic.taste1: The author describes the result as the long, clear aftertaste found in a good pour-over.

wendelboe.title: Tim Wendelboe’s Finca Tamana brew
wendelboe.summary: 36 g to 600 g of boiling water through a Cafec Abaca+ filter; the video demonstrates a rough bloom, swirl and aggressive remaining pour, with no total time.
wendelboe.equipment: Dripper not stated; Cafec Abaca+ paper filter
wendelboe.notes: The description gives only coffee, water and filter. In the video Wendelboe says the local boiling point at Finca Tamana is about 92–93 °C, uses the same grind setting for every coffee, blooms with roughly 100 g, swirls, waits about 30 seconds and pours the rest aggressively. These are video observations; approximate quantities stay out of the fixed fields.
wendelboe.finish: No total time is published. Stir before serving unless the coffee is poured into another vessel.
wendelboe.overview: A loose field method from Finca Tamana rather than a tightly specified recipe. The video adds the workflow the description omitted, while leaving grind, dripper model, exact pour pattern and total time open.
wendelboe.bestFor: A large cup using the exact text-layer constants and Wendelboe’s permissive field workflow
wendelboe.teach1: Start with freshly ground, high-quality coffee; Wendelboe treats that as part of the recipe, not an optional upgrade.
wendelboe.teach2: Use water he considers good enough to drink on its own.
wendelboe.teach3: The video shows roughly 100 g for the bloom, a swirl, about 30 seconds of waiting, then one aggressive pour for the remainder.
wendelboe.s00: Bloom with roughly 100 g, using enough water to wet all the grounds; the quantity is approximate in the video.
wendelboe.s01: Swirl gently to saturate the bed and level it.
wendelboe.s02: After about 30 seconds, pour the remaining water quite aggressively; no fixed spiral or pour pattern is prescribed.
wendelboe.teach4: Stir the coffee before serving unless you pour it into another container.

waterLevelRule: Keep the water {level} above the bed

glossaryIntro: Short explanations for specialist terms used above.

wdt.definition: A needle tool breaks up coffee clumps before brewing or tamping. Wet WDT means stirring the wet bloom with that tool.

melodrip.definition: A shower-head flow restrictor placed above the brewer to soften and spread the water stream.

tds.definition: Total dissolved solids, a concentration measurement for water or brewed coffee. It is not a taste score.

ppm.definition: Parts per million, a concentration unit. Water TDS and calcium-carbonate hardness are different measures.

redClix.definition: A Comandante grinder adjustment upgrade with finer click resolution. Click numbers apply only to that grinder setup.

vst.definition: A precision espresso filter basket. Its capacity and flow affect the suitable dose and grind.

linePressure.definition: The incoming water pressure before the machine applies its main extraction pressure. It is not the same as the stated 9 bar stage.

bypass.definition: Water that flows around rather than through the coffee bed. A no- or low-bypass brewer is designed to reduce that route.

w60.definition: A flat-bottom brewer used here with both its metal mesh and a paper filter; the source does not detail their assembly.

retiredRecipe.title: This recipe has been retired
retiredRecipe.body: The Coffee with April W60 film was an exploratory test, not a recommended recipe. April found mesh alone too silty and mesh plus paper cleaner but still flat and dull. The result is preserved in the W60 equipment record; this URL remains so existing links do not break.
